requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
**Verdict.** The requirement is met. The one weakness is a missing direct assertion on the declaration text, explained under Tests.

**Implementation.**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs, lines 50–206) carries `{impl}` for `requirements.authoring_input` and for `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
- It looks the subject up in the loaded definitions and rejects terms and unknown names.
- It seeds the selector list with `InputSelector::Requirements { requirements: subject_name }` before any other selector.
- That selector goes through `source_input` and is never removed. `generated_evidence_selector` omits only `Outline` selectors under `evidence/`, so `Requirements` selectors are never filtered out.
- The result is pushed into `mandatory`, which becomes the mandatory input set.
- `InputSelector::Requirements` resolves (src/inputs.rs, `resolve`) to the declaration's `raw_lines`. In `collect_definitions` these are the whole block from `block.start..block.end`, so they include the opening `:::{req}` or `:::{example}` fence and the closing `:::`. Only option lines are stripped, and other requirements specify that.
- `source_input` also applies the read-access check on the declaration file, so the declaration is a genuine mandatory input.
- The mandatory set is built in one place, so there is no code that implements part of this requirement without an `{impl}` marker.
- I found no behaviour in the marked code that this requirement or another cited definition fails to cover.

**Tests.**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (inputs.rs, line 599) prepares both a requirement subject (`requirements.ready`) and an example subject (`requirements.case`).
  - For the example it asserts `mandatory_inputs()[0]["requirements"] == "requirements.case"`, so the subject's own declaration is the first mandatory input.
  - It also checks that cited declarations are present and uncited ones are absent.
  - It checks that earlier evidence inputs are not carried forward.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` (inputs.rs, line 751) shows that `prepare` fails with a `git add` error when the declaration file `md/requirements.md` is unstaged. This confirms the declaration is a mandatory read.
- `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines` (src/evidence.rs, line 3096) checks that the `Requirements` selector resolves to the full fenced `raw_lines`, `[":::{req} ready", "Ready MUST hold.", "::: :"]`. It is cited for other requirements, not this one, but it covers the text-completeness link in the chain.
- The `prepare` tests do not assert the full fenced text of the subject input directly. That gap is minor, because the resolution path is separately tested and the subject's presence and position are asserted.

Overall the implementation is complete and exact, and the tests cover the design space adequately.
